Yesterday The Daily Mirror conducted important experiments with an aeroplane in flight on the Government flying ground at Lark Hill, Salisbury Plain. They are the first of their kind to be carried out in this country. Mr, Robert Loraine, the actor-airman, came down specially from London and made a flight, in the course of which he sent wireless messages from the aeroplane which were picked up at the

receiving station a quarter of a mile away. (1) Mr. Thorne Baker, The Daily Mirror scientific expert, holding the apparatus. (2) Mr. Thorne Baker (profile) explaining the working of the Morse key to Mr. Loraine. (3) Mr. Loraine in flight. He is sending a code-signal, meaning "Enemy in sight." (4) Mr. Thorne Baker listening for the signals with the Marconi receiver.-(Daily Mirror photographs.)

ENGLISH FREEDOM.
Should telephone girls be allowed to wear their hair over their ears? Judges of the Berlin courts have decided, after grave deliberation, that they may.

The case which elicited this decision was that of Fraulein Irene Tresch, a telephone girl who was dismissed because she insisted upon wearing a bande covering her ears. Her employer objected to this style of hairdressing on the ground that she was unable to apply the telephone receiver direct to her ears.
She brought an action for unjustifiable summary dismissal, appearing in court with bandeaux which only allowed a small portion of the lobe of the ear to be seen, and won her case.
The judges decided that a coiffure after the style of Cleo de Merode was not a sufficient reason for dismissal without notice.
